bullets.title: PLTR: Monster Q2 Beat—US Commercial +149% YoY, Stock +26%, Deutsche Bank Upgrades
bullets.body: Palantir reported Q2 revenue $1.94B (+7.2% above consensus), operating margin 61.7%, and raised FY guidance ~11 points; US Commercial growth accelerated to +149% YoY and US Government grew +90%. Deutsche Bank upgraded to Buy with $200 PT; Mizuho raised PT to $215 from $185 (Outperform); DA Davidson reiterates Buy citing 90% growth, 60% margins, and +150% net retention. Stock +26% intraday.

bullets.title: Optical ban catalyst: COHR +14%, LITE +11%, AAOI soaring on US Chinese data-center component import restrictions
bullets.body: Reuters reported the Trump administration is drafting a ban on imports of Chinese optical transceivers used in AI data centers (FCC rule expected this year), sending COHR +14%, LITE +11%, AAOI +17%, CIEN +9%, GLW +8% in pre/intraday trading. Morgan Stanley notes COHR is the clearest beneficiary via vertical integration; non-Chinese suppliers lack near-term capacity to fully backfill ~50% Chinese market share, and InP substrate supply from China (AXTI) is a critical bottleneck.

bullets.title: AMZN: Hits $3T market cap; Bezos files to sell ~$4B; NJ AG files antitrust suit—stock -2.5%
bullets.body: Amazon became the fifth company to cross $3 trillion market cap (joining NVDA, GOOGL, MSFT, AAPL), but pulled back ~2.5% on two overhangs: Bezos filed to sell up to 15M shares (~$4.07B of founder stock from 1994) and New Jersey AG Jennifer Davenport filed an antitrust lawsuit alleging Amazon abused market power over independent delivery drivers.

bullets.title: W: +20% on 2Q beat and stronger 3Q guide (high-single-digit growth vs mid-single-digit consensus)
bullets.body: Wayfair reported Q2 revenue $3.52B (+7.5% YoY), ~2% above consensus, adj. EBITDA $242M vs $230M consensus (6.9% margin). Q3 guidance was high-single-digit growth vs Street's ~+4.8%, driving the stock up ~20%. Perigold luxury +35%, specialty brands +20%; Citi maintains Buy with $95 PT.

bullets.title: SPOT: Q2 margin beat, 300M subscribers—but Q3 MAU guide (788M vs 793M consensus) weighs, stock -6%
bullets.body: Spotify hit 300M premium subscribers (+7M in Q2) and record gross margins of 33.4% (+193bps YoY) with FCF of €797M. However, Q3 total MAU guidance of 788M missed consensus ~793M and Q3 operating income guided €670M vs €678M Street; Morgan Stanley reiterates OW with $640 PT but Street broadly sidelined by opex concerns.

bullets.title: NVDA: Citi flags Rubin Ultra shifting to 8-Hi HBM4 (from 12-Hi) to scale GPU count to 576; pivot to scale-out
bullets.body: Citi reports NVIDIA is reportedly considering lowering Rubin Ultra HBM content from 12-Hi to 8-Hi (reducing per-GPU capacity 33% to 192GB), pivoting from scale-up to scale-out: Rubin Ultra NVL576 would expand NVLink domain from 72 to 576 GPUs, increasing aggregate HBM capacity by 433% to 110.6TB. HBM supply remains persistently tight as memory suppliers prioritize higher-margin alternatives.

bullets.title: CRWV/NBIS: Citi cuts PTs (CRWV to $142, NBIS to $278) but stays constructive—supply delays, not demand weakness
bullets.body: Citi reduced CRWV PT to $142 and NBIS PT to $278 after recent selloffs in the NeoCloud group, but remains constructive: delays are supply-side (permitting, NIMBY, costs) not demand-side, AI capacity is largely sold out, and project delays reinforce scarcity value. NVDA holds a 9.3% stake in NBIS; CRWV backlog growth expected to continue despite Meta capacity announcement.

bullets.title: ANET: F2Q26 earnings today—Street at $2.83B revenue, billings facing tough Q2 comp; new 52-week high
bullets.body: Arista reports today with consensus at F2Q26 revenue $2.83B (slightly above $2.8B guidance), GM 62.2%, EPS $0.89. Investors watching for billings growth (accelerated +54% YoY in F1Q26 vs tough $3.2B F2Q25 comp), FY26 guidance raise on big-tech capex, and supply/pricing commentary. ANET hit a new 52-week high (+2.6% on the day, +61.3% YTD).

bullets.title: SNAP: Q2 EBITDA beats by 29.5%; Specs launch Sept 16 overhang; Wells Fargo raises PT to $6
bullets.body: Snap reported Q2 revenue $1.60B (+3.8% above consensus) and adj. EBITDA $249.6M (+29.5% beat); non-advertising revenue surged 85% YoY. Q3 guidance implies ~7% ad growth (vs Q2's 9%) with EBITDA slightly light vs estimates. Wells Fargo raised PT to $6 from $5; sell-side mix is 23% Buy / 71% Hold. Stock +14.8% on the day.

bullets.title: NVDA/MU/SNDK: Memory 2027 capacity fully allocated; HBM could absorb 70% of DRAM capacity
bullets.body: Digitimes reports global DRAM and HBM capacity for 2027 is fully allocated; memory suppliers seeing only 60-70% order fulfillment vs requested volumes. MU, Samsung, SanDisk fully presold 2027 NAND capacity. Wolfe initiates SK Hynix ADR (SKHY) Outperform at $200 PT, noting DRAM supply/demand gap to widen in CY27 due to cleanroom constraints and rising HBM content doubling on Rubin Ultra in 2H27.

bullets.title: GOOGL/AVGO: Blackstone opens talks on ~$36B debt financing for Anthropic to buy Google TPU chips
bullets.body: Blackstone is in early talks with investors on a potential new debt financing package of at least $36B for Anthropic to purchase Google TPU chips—following the June $35B package. Broadcom is backstopping payments on the largest segments; separately, Anthropic signed a $10B deal with Volta for compute capacity in Norway, with NVDA and DELL as strategic investors in Volta.

bullets.title: NET: Cloudflare reports Q2 in line/beat; launches AI wallet payments; stock +10% since May, new 52-week high
bullets.body: Cloudflare's Q2 revenue $664.7M beat guidance midpoint, with FY26 revenue guided $2.81B in line with consensus; the stock hit a new 52-week high (+4.6% on the day, +47.8% YTD). Additionally, Cloudflare announced Cloudflare Wallets and cloudflare.pay, enabling AI agents to make purchases online with configurable spending caps and merchant whitelists.

bullets.title: TKO: Beat-and-raise; FY guidance raised $75M revenue and $25M EBITDA on World Cup and Freedom 250 upside
bullets.body: TKO raised FY guidance by $75M revenue and $25M adjusted EBITDA driven by World Cup demand and Freedom 250 upside; WWE results were in-line to slightly below consensus with Wrestlemania mix shifting toward international events. JPMorgan rates TKO Overweight with $222 PT.

bullets.title: BTDR: +10% on $4.7B, 16-year Tydal data center lease; 22% implied yield vs 18.6% sector high
bullets.body: Bit Digital announced a $4.7B revenue deal (extendable to $8B) over 16 years for its Tydal, Norway AI/HPC campus at $2.4M per MW with 90% NOI margin, implying a 22% yield vs the prior 18.6% sector high. Capex remaining is $4/watt vs $8-12/watt range; Morgan Stanley notes investors expect lower capex and higher yields going forward.

bullets.title: TSLA: China July deliveries +37.8% YoY to 93,579 units
bullets.body: Tesla China July deliveries rose 37.8% year-over-year to 93,579 units per CPCA/PCA preliminary data, signaling a strong demand recovery in its largest international market.

bullets.title: AAPL: DZ Bank downgrades to Hold from Buy, PT $310; India sales top $10B for first time
bullets.body: DZ Bank cut Apple to Hold from Buy with a $310 price target. Separately, Apple's annual sales in India exceeded $10 billion for the first time, underscoring the country's growing importance as a growth market. OpenAI also published message exchanges suggesting conflict with Apple over integration terms.

bullets.title: FOXA: Q4 earnings preview—$3.64B revenue, $1.44 EPS; Wolfe hosting callback webcast Aug 6
bullets.body: Fox Corp reports Q4 with consensus at $3.64B revenue (Cable $1.64B, TV $1.94B), EBITDA $1.0B, EPS $1.44. FOXA has beaten revenue consensus 17 of past 20 quarters; options imply ~7.5% move. Wolfe Research hosting 15-min callback webcast Aug 6 at 5:30pm ET.

bullets.title: AMD: Post-earnings webcast Aug 5 at 10:30am ET (Wolfe); focus on data center and connectivity demand
bullets.body: Wolfe Research is hosting a post-earnings AMD webcast on August 5 at 10:30am ET with management callback; Chris Caso hosting. Goldman Sachs notes all eyes on AMD and ANET today for data center and connectivity demand signals.

bullets.title: HUT: Q2 margins miss badly—EBITDA $10M vs $27M consensus; stock -4.8%, +144% YTD
bullets.body: Hut 8 reported Q2 results with EBITDA of only ~$10M versus consensus $27M (adjusted for digital asset mark-to-market changes), missing on margins. The stock is down ~4.8% on the day but remains +144% year-to-date.

bullets.title: ACN: UBS Buy—Qantas Project iQ AI transformation; share of enterprises preferring ACN as AI partner rises to 58%
bullets.body: UBS reiterates Buy on Accenture with $275 PT: Qantas is in advanced discussions for Project iQ, an AI transformation covering ~1,000 back-office positions. Accenture's share of large enterprises (>10k employees) identifying it as preferred AI implementation partner rose to 58% from 47% in October 2025, and only ~19% of enterprises have AI deployed at scale, implying a multi-year demand runway.
